title: Mirage
wikitext:
{{Update|reason=Changes from 3.30}} {{About|the league mechanic}} '''Mirages''', also known as "mirage areas", are a [[league mechanic]] introduced in [[Mirage league]]. Throughout Wraeclast, players can encounter a gateway to the Astral Realm, containing an imperfect copy of the current area holding a tortured captive djinn that must be released. Mirages can first be encountered in [[The Vastiri Desert]] and [[The Oasis]] in [[Act 9]] (in non-[[Ruthless mode]]). In the [[endgame]], Mirages have a chance to appear randomly in maps and can be guaranteed to appear via an explicit modifier. ==Mechanics== [[File:Free the Djinn.png|thumb|The djinn imprisoned in the non-instanced mirage before meeting Varashta for the first time.]] Areas contain a small non-instanced mirage containing some [[Afarud]] monsters. Defeating the Afarud monsters around the djinn (marked on the minimap) will summon the [[NPC]] [[Varashta, the Winter Sekhema]]. Speak to Varashta and select a Wish, the mirage, granting a choice between one of three random options that can modify the mirage's rewards or monsters or grant powerful buffs. In the endgame, each Wish is associated with one of three djinn (Ruzhan, Navira, and Kelari), which add an additional effect to the Mirage: * Sigil of Kelari: Monsters spawned by Astral Anomalies in Miraged Areas drop 500% increased Gold. * Sigil of Navira: Monsters spawned by Astral Anomalies in Miraged Areas are at least Magic. * Sigil of Ruzhan: 100% increased number of Astral Anomalies in Miraged Areas. After selecting a Wish, Varashta will summon a portal to enter the mirage. Entering will generate an imperfect copy of the parent area called a "mirage area"; this area has the same layout as the zone you entered it from. The first time you enter a mirage and deactivate [[Grace Period]], a shockwave is released around your character which stuns and knocks back nearby enemies. The mirage can be exited at any time by leaving through the portal; there is also a hotkey available that teleports the character to near the portal ({{key press|F7}} by default). Dying in the mirage area will send the player to their [[hideout]] while in [[map]]s, requiring a portal for re-entry. In voided maps (i.e. from [[Valdo's Map]]s), dying in a mirage will still [[void league|void]] the character. {{il|Portal Scroll|Portal Scrolls}} and other player-created portals are disabled in the mirage area. Mirages will duplicate most league mechanics that spawned in the original area, though not perfectly, which can result in changes to certain mechanics or rewards, described further below. In areas that contain mirages, many league mechanics that can be copied by the mirage will generally tend to spawn close to the mirage if possible. It will also copy unique monsters found in [[act]] areas or [[map boss]]es. * Instanced mechanics (e.g. Syndicate [[safehouse]]s, [[Labyrinth Trial]]s, [[Vaal side area]]s, [[Abyssal Depths]]) will not be duplicated by mirages. * Doors that transition to other areas in the map will not spawn, except for ones the leads to a boss arena. * [[Delirium|Mirrors of Delirium]], [[Sentinel]]s, and Demonic Evocators ([[Beyond]]) will spawn near the mirage entrance. * [[The Viridian Wildwood]] will not be duplicated by mirages. * [[Master]] missions will not be duplicated by mirages. * [[Eldritch altar]] can spawn in mirage areas, and their modifiers are not shared between the main map and the mirage area * Mirages in [[Valdo's map]]s do not duplicate Valdo's map rewards. Each mirage area contains an "Astral Chain" which holds a djinn trapped, surrounded by one or more magic or rare enemies. Killing the Rare monsters guarding the Astral Chain will destroy it, completing the mirage encounter. Wishes that spawn an Astral Cache will do so near the Astral Chain's location after competing the mirage; otherwise, it will spawn a Bronze, Silver, or Gold Djinn's Cache containing random items. Mirage areas also contains several [[Afarud]] monster packs that can drop [[Afarud unique]]s or [[Restored Maraketh unique]]s. Additionally, shimmering purple mirages can be found in the area; approaching one will typically spawn a pack of Afarud monsters and sometimes also a Bronze, Silver, or Gold Djinn's Cache. In Tier 14+ [[map]]s, mirage encounters (inside or outside of a mirage) may sometimes spawn the unique monster [[Ridan, Afarud Commander]]. When killed, he drops {{il|The Black Barya}}. The Black Barya is required to access the [[Saresh, of the Weeping Black]] boss encounter. Wish for Rust will cause Ridan to be guaranteed to spawn after destroying the mirage's Astral Chain. When [[map boss]]es duplicated in a mirage area, they gain the {{c|white|Astral-touched}} modifier. This causes them to periodically unleash a nova that deals damage and inflicts a slowing debuff. Duplicated map bosses will grant Atlas completion for the current map even if the original map boss is not defeated. Additionally, they can be witnessed by the [[Maven]] or drop [[Eldritch Horror]] invitations. Notably, defeating the Mirage final map boss first before the regular final map boss will cause it to drop two Eldritch Horror invitations; this does not work in the reverse order. ===Wishes=== [[File:Fountain of Wealth screenshot.png|200px|thumb|A Fountain of Wealth.]] * Djinn sigils are introduced upon entering [[map]]s. * Wish for Glyph can be combined with {{il|Perandus Signet}} to have up to a 9% chance to drop an extra {{il|Scroll of Wisdom}} on kill with {{psl|The Unseen Hand}}. * Wish for Terror can summon a random boss from {{il|Maven's Invitation: The Feared}}. Defeating this boss has a chance to drop a unique item from their drop pool (regular version, not Uber). * Wish for Elements grants {{stl|Blessing of the Storm}} buff, which grants {{c|mod|Elemental Ailments you inflict spread to other Enemies}} and {{c|mod|All Damage you deal can Chill, Shock and Ignite}}. * Wish for Oases creates [[Oasis ground]], which grant 10% of Life and Mana regenerated per second while standing on it. * Wish for Pursuit creates Golden Volatiles, are orbs of golden coins that flee from the character. Touching one causes it to turn into a pile of Gold. * Wish for Prosperity contains a Fountain of Wealth that when clicked, drops several piles of Gold, and generates many Golden Volatiles. * Wish for Betrayal spawns [[Immortal Syndicate]] members identically to {{il|Allflame Ember of Kulemak}}. They have a very high chance to drop a random [[scarab]] when killed, and revive after killing the map boss. * Wish for Rust has an approximately 4% chance to appear in a map.
